correctness.rationale: Normalize the two Jordan parts of the circular derivative by V/2, and pair them to express the function modulo constants as a probability average of oriented arc indicators times V/2. Equality can be checked by the Hilbert-space variance identity: the residuals must all equal one maximizing residual. The multiplier 1−sinc²(πka) is nonzero for k≠0, so equality of residuals identifies the arc modulo constants. For the arc energy F(L), expansion of (I−T_a)^2 gives F(L)=L+2∫₀ᴸ(L−x)(K_a*K_a−2K_a)(x)dx, using circular kernels. The unwrapped four-box spline gives F(az)=aΦ(z) for z≤1; no translate contributes even at a=1/3 and z=1. The quartic is strictly convex with opposite endpoint signs and has exactly one root on (0,1). Beyond a, F''≥0 all the way to 1/2 even with wrapping, so F'≤0 by symmetry. The strict decrease from ar to a rules out every other length except the complementary one. For a≤1/4 integration of the outer spline gives the a/5 plateau; V=2 for a unit arc gives the claimed squared-norm factor 1/4. Exact independent spline-integral, root-enclosure and plateau checks passed; replay from /workspace with python3 -I -B branches/frozen_review_checks.py.
residual_risks: The finite checks supplement the exact proof. Nothing is established for a>1/3, a forward-shifted residual, or another norm.
